subject: Post-call: model recommendations, acceptance gates & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finscale.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed evaluation plan

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and an actionable plan so we can move to a short qualification eval next week.

What we agreed on (recap)
- Scope: NLU & synthesis flows for your ‘payment reconciliation’ product (3 canonical intents + 4 contextual summarization prompts).
- Success criteria: prefer open-model parity to your current proprietary baseline (FinScale-Base-1.5) but will accept a clear fallback plan if parity isn't achieved.
- Timeline: 2-week sandbox evaluation window starting Monday 11/16.

Recommended next steps (what Redwood will do)
1) Run a controlled benchmark over your red-teamed sample set (attached: finscale_sample_prompts_v1.csv). We'll run three candidate model families:
   - LlamaX-13B (quantized FP16) — open candidate (fast iteration).
   - OpenLM-7B-v2 (8-bit Q) — lower cost baseline.
   - Redwood-7B-prop — our proprietary baseline for parity comparison and fallback.
2) Provide both automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not ideal here — we'll use task-specific accuracy/F1 and hallucination rate) and a 50-case human acceptability sample.
3) Pragmatic acceptance gates (proposal):
   - Task-specific macro-F1 >= 0.82 (relative to FinScale-Base-1.5) OR
   - Human acceptability >= 88% AND hallucination rate <= 6%
   - Latency SLO: 95th percentile <= 420ms for short prompts (we'll profile on your target region).
4) Deliverables by 11/30: a one-page readout, full metric spreadsheet, sample model outputs, and a recorded walkthrough.

What we need from you
- Confirm NDA + sandbox access (we'll send a short DocuSign if needed).
- Confirm the sample CSV is the right slice (I attached what you dropped in the call). If you'd prefer a different subset for the human-review bucket, tell us which row ids.

Attachments: finscale_sample_prompts_v1.csv, finscale_security_qs.pdf, redwood_eval_plan_template.xlsx

I'll loop Rishi on the evaluation config and Neha on security/compliance gating. If this looks right, we'll kick off infra provisioning first thing Monday.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finscale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finscale.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed evaluation plan

Marissa — thanks, that structure looks good. A few clarifications from our side before you start: 

1) Cost/latency: can you provide an estimated per-1k-token cost for each candidate model with the suggested quantization, and a rough expected 95p latency on an m6g-like instance? Important since we run heavy concurrency on peak times.
2) Hallucination gate: can you clarify how you compute hallucination rate? Is that strictly factuality vs the ground truth field in the CSV or will reviewers label hallucination per response?
3) Human review: Priya asks whether you can provide an example rubric for the 50-case human acceptability review.

If those answers are reasonable, we can confirm sandbox access. Also — we prefer the subset rows 101-600 for the automated pass and 601-650 for human review.

—Alex
Alex Chen | Head of Product, FinScale
alex.chen@finscale.com | +1 (212) 555-0987
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finscale.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed evaluation plan

Alex, Priya — great questions. Quick answers and the plan for measurement (I'll run the config once we have sandbox creds):

1) Cost & latency (estimates)
   - LlamaX-13B (8-bit Q) — estimated cost ~ $0.60 / 1k tokens, expected 95p latency ~ 380-450ms depending on prompt length and concurrency.
   - OpenLM-7B-v2 (8-bit Q) — estimated cost ~ $0.35 / 1k tokens, expected 95p latency ~ 340-420ms.
   - Redwood-7B-prop — estimated cost ~ $0.95 / 1k tokens, expected 95p latency ~ 300-380ms.
   Notes: exact numbers depend on batch sizing; we'll run profiling with your concurrency setting (please specify typical concurrent requests during peak).

2) Hallucination measurement
   - Automated pass: we compute token-level overlap plus a conservative string-match on known reference values in the CSV (IDs/amounts/invoice refs). This flags obvious hallucinations.
   - Human review: reviewers will mark each response as OK / Minor Issue / Hallucination. Hallucination rate = (# responses labeled Hallucination) / (total reviewed). We'll include examples in the rubric.

3) Human rubric (summary)
   - Correctness: Is the core factual element present and accurate? (OK / Minor / Hallucination)
   - Relevance: Is the response focused on the asked intent? (Yes/No)
   - Conciseness & actionability: 0-2 score
   - Final pass threshold for 'acceptability' = >= 88% OK across the 50-case sample.

4) Acceptance gating and fallback policy (operational)
   - If an open model reaches the F1 target but exceeds hallucination gate by up to 2 percentage points, we can run a straight-through filter that falls back to Redwood-7B-prop for high-risk intents (e.g., invoice reconciliation).
   - If open models miss both F1 and human acceptability, Redwood will provide a rollback/fallback plan and recommend either targeted prompt engineering or using Redwood-7B-prop for the failing intents.

5) Execution plan & ask from FinScale
   - Please provide concurrency target (e.g., 50 rps peak), and confirm the row ranges Alex requested (101-600 auto, 601-650 human).
   - Sandbox API keys and the lightweight S3 bucket with the sample set (read-only) so we can run evals.

Links we will publish in the readout
- Internal benchmark dashboard (read-only): https://redwood.app/internal/benchmarks/open-vs-prop/FS-089-report
- Evaluation config repo (prompt sets + seed): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_redwood_finscale_eval

We will start with the LlamaX-13B and OpenLM-7B runs in parallel and hold Redwood-7B-prop as the comparative baseline. I'll ping when the first automated pass completes (expected 48 hours after sandbox access).

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Principal ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
